Subject: Pilot sizing: expected token surges + SLO target

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited to move forward with a small pilot (production-facing) for our conversational agent. Before we lock the POC dates we need a concrete runbook from Redwood showing:

- Estimated tokens/sec at peak and how that maps to Dedicated GPU slabs (N units).
- Whether Redwood Dedicated can meet our latency SLO: 95th percentile \u2264 250ms for responses up to 512 tokens.
- A short fallback strategy if demand spikes beyond committed capacity (model variant + routing).

Quick profile attached (anvil_tps_profile.csv) — key points:
- Typical daytime steady-state: ~450k tokens/hour (~125 tokens/sec).
- Peak momentary bursts: sustained 3-4 minutes at ~6,500 tokens/sec (we believe this is due to promo traffic).
- Daily total (est): 3.2M tokens.

Pilot scope: 2-week production pilot, public user traffic, telemetry required (latency by endpoint, token counts).

Can you send a short playbook (assumptions + GPU mapping + headroom margin) we can use in our internal readiness review? We need it by EOD Friday to keep our timeline.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Ops, Anvil AI
E: ellen@anvil.ai
A: ops@anvil.ai

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot sizing: expected token surges + SLO target

Ellen — thanks for the profile and the clear ask. Attaching a short runbook summary here in the thread. Priyom, can you validate the GPU mapping and the fallback variant choices? Marissa, flagging for commercial (pilot sizing and pricing).

High-level assumptions we used (to be explicit):
- Model: open-llm-13B (baseline) — single-token latencies measured on our A100-like SKU (quantized path).
- Response size: up to 512 tokens. We budget per-request prompt + gen = 700 tokens on average for compute planning.
- Target SLO: p95 \u2264 250ms end-to-end (inference only). Network and app-layer budgets are assumed separate.
- Safety margin: plan for 40% headroom above observed peak for pilot (operationally conservative for bursty traffic).

Preliminary numbers (rough):
- Observed peak in your CSV: 6,500 tokens/sec.
- With 40% headroom -> planning target = 9,100 tokens/sec.
- On our A100-like SKU with optimized kernels and batching, effective throughput per GPU for the profile (700-token average per request) is ~1,400 tokens/sec for p95 <= 250ms (continuous load).
- GPUs required = ceil(9,100 / 1,400) = 7 GPUs. Recommend reserving a slab of 8 GPUs for pilot (1-GPU buffer for node failover/rolling updates).

Fallback strategy (quick):
- Canary route: route 10% of requests to quantized 8-bit variant (0.8x cost) with slightly higher latency, keep 90% on baseline.
- Automatic overflow: when queue depth or measured p95 moves above 250ms, divert new sessions to hosted variant with higher concurrency and throttle requests to committed slab.

Deliverables I'm attaching: short runbook (this thread), a unit-cost estimate, and a requested_slo_matrix.xlsx with alternative GPU counts.

I'll pause here — Priyom, can you confirm the per-GPU throughput assumption and any sequence-length sensitivities we should call out?

Best,
Dave
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: requested_slo_matrix.xlsx

Thanks Dave and Ellen — I ran a quick microbenchmark using the exact payload profile Ellen attached and a proxied workload (mix of 1-3 prompt tokens + gen up to 512). Notes below:

Benchmark assumptions and results:
- Hardware baseline: Redwood "rA100-80GB" equivalent, optimized kernel path, FP16+KV cache warm.
- Average request cost for sample traces: 0.45 GPU-seconds per 700-token transaction at p95 ~ 220ms (when scheduled with our continuous-batching policy and target concurrency).
- Effective sustained tokens/sec per GPU (700-token average) = 1,555 tokens/sec (slightly better than Dave's conservative 1,400).
- However, latency jitter on cold-started KV-caches increases p95 by ~35-50ms for first N requests when a new model shard is used; warm-up policy needed.

Revised plan and playbook (pilot):
- Planning target (40% headroom): 9,100 tokens/sec -> GPUs required (conservative) = ceil(9,100 / 1,500) = 7 GPUs. Recommend ordering an 8-GPU slab for pilot (same conclusion as Dave).
- Warm-up: run a rolling cache-warmup with synthetic prefix traffic 15 minutes before peak windows; this reduces first-request jitter. I'll include a warmup script.
- Autoscale/burst: allow 2x burst on top of slab via pre-warmed short-lived burst pool (e.g., spare spot/ephemeral nodes) with throttling rules to prevent SLA spill. For a 2x burst policy, we can absorb up to ~18,200 tokens/sec for short windows (60-180s) before redirect.
- Canary routing: start with 5% diverted traffic to quantized 8-bit variant (works well on the same slab and increases headroom by ~20% but with degraded quality).

Operational checklist (short):
- Confirm commit: pilot slab size (8 GPUs) and standby burst policy.
- Provide 72-hour sync window for warm-up prior to public launch.
- Instrumentation: token-level counters, per-route p50/p95/p99, and KV-cache hit rate exported to your dashboard.

I'll attach the warmup script and a CSV mapping tokens/sec -> estimated cost.

—Priyom
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: anvil_warmup.sh (script stub), anvil_cost_map.csv (tokens->$ estimate)
